name: btp-localhost-on-premise-access
description: Run and deploy a SAPUI5 or SAP Fiori elements app, or work in ABAP with ADT and ADT MCP servers, from your own machine through on-premise SAP BTP destinations. Claude sets up a local proxy that reaches the Cloud Connector through a cf ssh tunnel, and logs in to Cloud Foundry with a password from an environment variable.

cf_api.title: Cloud Foundry API endpoint
cf_api.description: Default region for new environments, e.g. https://api.cf.eu10.hana.ondemand.com (subaccount overview in the BTP cockpit)

cf_app.title: Tunnel app
cf_app.description: Default app bound to the destination and connectivity services (cf ssh goes through it)

cf_user.title: Cloud Foundry user (e-mail)
cf_user.description: User the scripts log in with when the cf session has expired

cf_password_env.title: Password variable
cf_password_env.description: NAME of the environment variable that holds that user's password, e.g. CF_PASSWORD. Set the variable in your shell profile: the password itself never goes into this configuration

cf_origin.title: Identity provider origin
cf_origin.description: Only for a custom identity provider (cf auth --origin), e.g. sap.custom; empty for the SAP ID service

cf_sso.title: Log in with single sign-on
cf_sso.description: Use an SSO passcode instead of user and password. The scripts cannot log in again on their own then: an expired session needs cf login --sso in a terminal
